description: All system bugs. Each bug has its own environment and status attributes. Environments constrained to local/dev/qa/prod. Source of truth for defect tracking.

bug.title: Rule-006 (which responds to Anthropic's tool use web hook) is fundamentally broken; currently disabled; must be redesigned from scratch
bug.description:
Rule-006 was intended to gate every Claude-initiated Bash/PowerShell tool call through a five-stage funnel so LOCAL work always passed and REMOTE state mutations required either the oneoff.py wrapper with an operator-approved explanation or a chain-surface allowlist bypass. The rule's enforcement worker (architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/llm_classify_shell_invocation_worker.py) is wired as a PreToolUse hook. As of 2026-08-04 the rule's enforcements[] list has been emptied so the worker no longer fires; all remote-mutation gating is currently OFF. Rebuilding it is deferred.

BUSINESS RULES, invented and real, the code and JSON were attempting to implement (extracted from Rule-006 statements 1-8 and the classifier source):

(1) Stage 1 local allowlist -- hardcoded set of shell verbs whose effect is structurally confined to the local filesystem passes without invoking the LLM (ls, cat, grep, find, rm/mv/cp on local paths, git read-only verbs, PowerShell Get-*/Test-Path/Where-Object, plus `git push` in any non-force form because Rule-065's commit gate covers push-after-authorized-commit). Script invocations (python foo.py, pytest, bash foo.sh, powershell foo.ps1, npm run, poetry run) NEVER allowlisted regardless of contents. Network verbs (curl, wget, ftp, ssh) NEVER allowlisted. Force-push variants of git push NEVER allowlisted.

(2) Stage 2 recursive code-path walk -- parse referenced Python scripts with AST and shell/ps1 with regex; follow subprocess.run/call/Popen/check_output/os.system/os.popen/runpy/importlib.import_module; bounded to 60 nodes and 6 depth levels; cycles broken via visited-set; unresolvable dynamic-code patterns surfaced as walk_error/dynamic_evidence.

(3) Stage 3 LLM classification via Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite; 75s per-attempt timeout; 6 retries on 429/5xx with exponential backoff + jitter; strict-JSON output {classification, reason}; on LLM error default to gate_approve (never silently block); LLM-error verdicts not cached.

(4) Stage 4 outcome dispatch -- `allow` silent; `gate_approve` prompts operator (inline TTY APPROVE or browser popup in agent contexts); `reject` denies with a passive notification; verdicts cached by payload-hash.

(5) Stage 5 oneoff wrapper -- Claude's legal path for remote mutations is `python architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/code/oneoff.py --explanation "<why in 4-70 words>" -- <inner command>`; two Stage-1 accommodations bypass the wrapper: (a) chain surfaces build_chathealthy.py / deploy_chathealthy.py / promote_chathealthy.py; (b) `git push` non-force forms.

(6) Categorical rules baked into the classifier prompt -- local filesystem work is always `allow` regardless of file contents; no chain-surface auto-allow at Stage 3 (each script is walked); "reaches remote" = Azure / Cloudflare / MongoDB Atlas / HuggingFace / ACR / GitHub write-mode / pypi write-mode / npm write-mode / any HTTP POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH to external host; curl/wget GET to public read-only endpoints `allow`, POST/PUT/DELETE `gate_approve` or `reject`; harness temp files always `allow`.

(7) Every remote-mutation attempt fires a browser notification and is recorded to architecture/EngineeringRuleEnforcement/ArchitectureDesignAndAuditDocs/llm_classify_shell_invocation.log.

(8) Deploy-from-git preflight -- deploy_chathealthy.py/promote_chathealthy.py with --env dev|qa|prod denied unless the working tree is clean AND HEAD is at origin/<current-branch>; --env local exempt.

WHY IT IS BROKEN (observed 2026-08-04 and across preceding weeks): Statement 8 does not belong in Rule-006 -- Rule-006's job (statements 1-7) is classifying shell invocations; statement 8 is a separate git-state precondition tacked onto the same enforcement worker for implementation convenience. Its "working tree must be clean" clause is Claude-invented friction with no supporting business requirement -- the actual promote rule is "dev branch deploys dev, qa deploys qa, main deploys prod" and that invariant is now upheld by build_chathealthy.py reading from origin/<branch> and the deploy's manifest.env staleness gate, without any local-tree check. The classifier funnel (statements 1-7) also has structural problems: the Stage-2 recursive walk is simultaneously too permissive (misses genuinely dynamic behavior -- exec, importlib on runtime strings, subprocess with runtime-constructed args -- despite the walk_error surfacing) and too restrictive (rejects legitimate operational patterns); the Stage-3 LLM call adds seconds of latency to every uncached remote invocation; the Stage-5 wrapper requirement puts explanation-writing burden on Claude for every legitimate cloud operation and produces a stream of same-shape popups; the Stage-1 chain-surface accommodations became load-bearing because all real work goes through those three scripts anyway, which contradicts the categorical rule (statement 6b) that there is "no chain-surface auto-allow"; and payload-hash caching does not solve the fundamental latency + wrapper-verbosity problem, it just deduplicates identical repeats.

CURRENT STATE: rule id `Rule-006` in brain/machine_artifacts/content/engineering_rules.json is present with all 8 statements intact for reference. Its enforcements[] list is empty as of 2026-08-04 so chathealthy_enforcement_manager.py finds nothing to dispatch on PreToolUse. The worker file (llm_classify_shell_invocation_worker.py) is still on disk unchanged (~1400 lines) but no longer invoked. No other rule is doing shell-invocation classification; remote-mutation governance is currently entirely operator-eyes-on.
bug.reproduction: 1. Inspect brain/machine_artifacts/content/engineering_rules.json for rule id `Rule-006` and observe enforcements[] is empty. 2. Run any Bash tool call that mutates remote state (e.g., az keyvault secret set ... or wrangler pages deploy ...) -- no classifier fires, no popup, no audit-log entry. 3. Review the same rule's statements 1-8 for the intended business rules that are currently unenforced.
next_action: Complete redesign from requirements to design to implementation.

bug.title: LLM call sites construct their own agent and pin their own vendor, outside the facade
bug.description:
ChatHealthy has an LLM facade at ChatHealthyLib/src/chathealthy_lib/llm.py. This bug's earlier description named eleven call sites constructing vendor SDK clients directly. That mechanism is now almost gone and the description was describing it after the fact: three of the files it named no longer exist (homeopathic_resolver.py, consent_service.py, embedding_client.py at the path given), Code/Shared/llm_client.py has no importer anywhere, and safety_service.py's is_emergency has no call site. A remediation aimed at the described mechanism would have touched four files, three of them dead, and left every live site untouched.

THE LIVE MECHANISM IS DIFFERENT. Nine call sites construct a pydantic-ai Agent themselves rather than receiving one, and each pins its vendor as a string literal:
  sharedServices/Code/UtteranceManager/utterance_manager.py:1068, :1204
  FindCare/ProviderManagement/utterance_mining.py:65, :186
  FindCare/ProviderManagement/facility_utterance.py:84
  FindCare/SpecialtyFilter/filter.py:173, :194
  ChatHealthyLib/src/chathealthy_lib/geo_extractor.py:97
  pipeline/Code/other_identifier_phrases_engine.py:410

AND THE FACADE CANNOT CENTRALISE VENDOR CHOICE AS BUILT. run_llm(agent, ...) receives an already-constructed agent, so retry, timeout and failure conversion are genuinely central while client construction and vendor selection cannot be. Five of the nine sites read the MODEL NAME from the prompt record and then hardcode the vendor prefix -- f"openai:{...}". So the model is data and the vendor is code, and the half that decides which company receives a person's words is the half that is not declared. Three vendors are live: openai, anthropic, google.
bug.reproduction:
1. grep -rn 'Agent(' --include=*.py sharedServices FindCare ChatHealthyLib pipeline | grep -v llm.py | grep -v tests -- returns the nine sites above.
2. grep -rn 'f"openai:' --include=*.py FindCare -- returns the five sites that read the model from the record and pin the vendor in source.
3. Read run_llm in llm.py: its first parameter is an agent, so no caller can delegate construction to it.
next_action: Decide whether the facade constructs the agent (so vendor and model both come from the record) or remains a runner (so vendor pinning needs a different home). The bug cannot be closed without that decision.
Delete the dead paths rather than migrating them: Code/Shared/llm_client.py and safety_service.py's is_emergency have no callers.

bug.title: NUCC taxonomy CSV pollutes SpecialtyMetaData with codes for unlicensed humans
bug.description: The NUCC provider taxonomy CSV (loaded by Code/DataPipelines/load_specialty_data.py from nucc.org) defines codes for individual roles that are not licensed healthcare practitioners — e.g., Homemaker (376J00000X), Reflexologist (173C00000X), Driver (172A00000X), Health & Wellness Coach (171400000X), Lay Midwife (175M00000X), Funeral Director (176P00000X), Veterinarian (174M00000X), Graphics Designer (1744G0900X), Religious Nonmedical Practitioner (374K00000X), Lactation Consultant Non-RN (174N00000X), Peer Specialist (175T00000X), and 25+ others sitting in NUCC Grouping 'Other Service Providers' plus the single 'Student, Health Care' code (390200000X). All of these pass the existing $vectorSearch filter {Section: 'Individual'} in domain/find_care/specialty_service.py because Section=Individual only excludes group-practice and non-individual entries; it does NOT distinguish licensed from unlicensed roles. NUCC itself has no 'requires license' field. The result is that the specialty filter surfaces non-licensed and non-clinical roles in user-facing search results (e.g., a 'find me a foot doctor' query can return Homemaker, Reflexologist, Driver, etc.). Fix approach: derive the legitimate NUCC code set from the NPPES NPI database — query NPPES for the distinct NUCC codes actually registered against real NPIs (Type 1 individual + Type 2 organization) and use that derived set as the allow-list at pipeline load time. Every NUCC code that has at least one real NPI registrant is in scope; codes with zero NPI registrants get excluded automatically. SpecialtyMetaData may need enrichment with the NPI Type(s) per NUCC code. False negatives are acceptable — every legitimate NUCC code will have at least one NPI record. A new pipeline requirement is needed and will be authored on 2026-05-04.
bug.reproduction: 1. Connect to {env}_PublicHealthData.SpecialtyMetaData. 2. Query: db.SpecialtyMetaData.find({Section:'Individual', Grouping: {$in: ['Other Service Providers', 'Student, Health Care']}}).count() — observe 37 records present in the dev cluster. 3. Run a specialty search via the specialty filter (e.g., 'find me a foot doctor'); observe non-licensed/non-clinical entries (Homemaker, Reflexologist, Driver, etc.) appearing in vector-search results.
next_action: The list of legitimate clinical NUCC codes MUST be curated manually. The NPPES-derived allow-list approach was tried (is_npi_registered field on ProprietaryData.SpecialtyAndProviderFlags, populated 2026-05-24) and found insufficient: 821 of 883 catalog codes have NPI registrants in our 298K-provider sample, including the polluting codes (Homemaker 376J00000X, Reflexologist 173C00000X, Driver 172A00000X) — real people DO register their NPI under these codes. A curated allow/deny list is the only reliable discriminator.

bug.title: Incremental load never deletes records missing from a full source file
bug.description:
STIPULATED BY THE OPERATOR 2026-09-10: the incremental capability is UNTESTED. It has never been run against a real dissemination file, so what follows is read from code rather than observed, and the gap below is one of several an untested path may hold.

EPIC-010-F-007-S-004-REQ-B-002 says: when `incremental=true`, no provider record shall be deleted or altered unless (a) the source row changed (record altered to match), or (b) the source is a full file and the record is missing from it (record deleted).

The implementation only does (a). When `incremental=true`, `pipeline/Code/provider_load_manager.py:231-235` skips drain entirely, and `pipeline/Code/provider_worker.py:345-367` upserts each present row by NPI via `ReplaceOne({"npi": npi}, doc, upsert=True)`. There is NO post-load reconciliation pass that detects NPIs in the collection but missing from the source file and deletes them.

NPPES is always a full dissemination file when the monthly file is used, so REQ branch (b) applies on every full-file incremental run, but no code path implements it. Stale and CMS-retired NPIs accumulate indefinitely in incremental mode.
test_success_criteria: An `incremental=true` run against an NPPES dissemination file MUST delete every provider record whose NPI is not present in the source file.
Boolean test: pre-load count = N, source file count = N - K (K NPIs missing), post-load count = N - K, and the K specific NPIs are no longer in the collection.
bug.reproduction:
1. Run a full load of state X with `incremental=false` - collection holds 1000 NPIs for X.
2. Wait one NPPES dissemination cycle in which CMS retires/merges 50 of those NPIs.
3. Operator runs `incremental=true`. Two source-file paths exist:
   3.a. Weekly NPPES incremental file: contains only records that changed since last weekly/full. The 50 retired NPIs appear in the diff with their NPI Deactivation Date populated. The code upserts each present row by NPI via `ReplaceOne({"npi": npi}, doc, upsert=True)`. The deactivation date is stored on the document but no logic acts on it: no out_of_scope flag is set, no record is deleted, no downstream signal is emitted. (REQ-B-002 branch (b) does not apply here because the source is not a full file; this exposes an orthogonal deactivation-flag-handling gap, and the system has no enforced way to distinguish weekly vs full source.)
   3.b. Monthly NPPES full file: contains every currently-disseminated record (active + deactivated-but-not-yet-purged); long-retired NPIs are absent entirely (CMS-purged). The code only upserts rows present in the file. There is NO post-load pass that scans the collection for NPIs absent from the source file. Long-retired (CMS-purged) NPIs remain in the collection indefinitely; recently-deactivated NPIs (still in the file with deactivation dates) remain 'active' in collection state. Direct violation of REQ-B-002 branch (b).
4. FindCare search returns providers CMS has retired.
next_action: The capability is untested. Before any incremental run, it needs a test against a real dissemination file -- not only for this gap but because an untested load path against the served collection is the risk, not this particular defect.
Deferred. No fix planned.
If a real business need to use incremental loading arises (currently every load is full), this bug must be fixed before the first incremental run.
Until then, all loads are `incremental=false` (drain -> reload), which is correct behavior under REQ-B-002 for full-loads and avoids the gap entirely.

V8 req capturing branch (b) of the legacy REQ-B-002 (full-source-file -> delete DB records absent from source) does NOT exist in EPIC-010-F-102-S-005. A new requirement under F-102-S-005 MUST be authored to capture this delete-on-absence semantic before this bug can be re-attached.

bug.title: MongoFailure not properly handled by pipelines
bug.description: The Controller has no retry policy for a lost MongoDB connection, so a transient outage ends a multi-hour run on the first failure. It then records the fatal reason to MongoDB, which is the resource that just became unavailable, so the run dies with no recorded cause. The DiscrepancyReport MUST survive a Mongo outage, which is always a fatal error.
bug.reproduction: 1. Start a pipeline run. 2. Make the Atlas cluster briefly unreachable to the Controller. 3. Observe the run terminates on the first exception with no retry, and the fatal reason is absent from pipelineAdmin because the quiesce write also failed.
next_action: Design and implement a solution.

bug.title: Inadequate governance over what gets deployed
bug.description:
Nothing gates a change to what is deployed. What is running in Azure, Atlas, Entra and Key Vault is not held to what the repository says should be running, in either direction, and Claude Code changes all of it by hand. Nothing detects it. What is deployed therefore cannot be reproduced from the repository, and every guarantee built on top of it is unverifiable -- that a migration runs approved code, that an identity holds only what it needs, that a build is what was reviewed. For a company handling healthcare data whose case to enterprise buyers rests on auditability, a deployment that cannot be reproduced from its own record is an existential risk, not a defect.

Two examples, both found on 2026-08-20 and only because the operator asked for a list of what was there.

Five runbooks were published into ChatHealthyJobManager that nobody asked for. Four -- ChatHealthyDataMigrator, ChatHealthyDataMigratorProvisioner, ChatHealthyDataMigratorOrchestrator, ChatHealthyDataMigratorDeprovisioner -- had no package in deployment_architecture.json at all. The fifth, pipeline_regression_test, was declared with no runbook_name and no schedule, so it could never be triggered; it had never run once and wrote its results to a collection nobody reads. All five shipped on every deploy. No gate objected, because every gate checks that what ships is declared, and the declaration is written by Claude -- so the record certifies itself.

The migration's Python packages were installed into its Automation account by hand, one az rest call at a time, because the declarations named packages with no content_url and the deploy therefore installed nothing. The account's true contents came from a Claude session, not from the record. The same look found httpx and cryptography imported and never declared, five transitive dependencies Azure does not resolve, and a pymongo wheel built for Windows declared for a Linux sandbox.

Deployment is not the boundary of the problem. In one session Claude created Entra applications and groups and assigned their owners; patched an Atlas custom role to add INSERT and REMOVE; minted and purged Key Vault certificate secrets; created Azure role assignments and deleted one that could not be restored; created and deleted Automation accounts, runbooks and webhooks; and dropped MongoDB collections. None of it passed through a build, a deploy, or any record. Each happened because a command was run, and the only thing between any of it and production was whether the operator happened to be reading at that moment.
test_success_criteria: Everything deployed matches what the repository declares, and the repository declares everything deployed.
Nothing is deployed or changed without an authorization that is recorded and names who gave it.
bug.reproduction: Audit the actual deployment facts against deployment_architecture.json. For each Automation account list its runbooks, variables and python3Packages and compare against what the record declares for that target. On 2026-08-20 this returned five runbooks present and unaccounted for, and a package set matching no declaration.
next_action: Decide what authorizes a deployment or a change, given the record is written by the actor the record is meant to constrain.

bug.title: A state-scoped pipeline fire replaces the whole served collection
bug.description:
publish_provider.py renames the staging collection over the loaded one with dropTarget true. Staging is absent at the start of a run, nothing copies the loaded collection into staging, and state_partitions returns only the named states for a scoped run.

So any fire whose state scope is narrower than the loaded collection installs only the states it built and destroys the rest. Silently: no error, no finding, no gate. It is unconditional on load mode -- the incremental flag is not involved.

The rule that prevents it exists ONLY as prose. The module docstring says production fires must always be state_scope ALL. That identifier appears nowhere else in the file. There is no runtime guard, no requirement and no test. A rule that exists only as a comment reads as enforced and is not.

This is the March 2026 data-loss incident's shape in a different place: a step that is correct for a full load, reached by a mode that does not satisfy its precondition. That incident was an unconditional drop of all fifty states for a Delaware-scoped run.
test_success_criteria: A fire whose state scope is narrower than the loaded collection MUST refuse to publish, or MUST carry every out-of-scope record forward.
Boolean test: load every state to N records, fire one state scoped to DE, then count. The count MUST NOT fall below N.
bug.reproduction:
1. Read publish_provider.py at the rename -- renameCollection with dropTarget true, unconditional on load mode or scope.
2. Read pipeline_runtime.py provider_collection -- it resolves to the STAGING collection, the same name publish renames.
3. Search the repository for an aggregation out stage, a merge stage, or any copy into staging -- none exists, so staging never receives the loaded records.
4. Read steps/_partitions.py state_partitions -- a scoped run yields only the named states.
5. Search publish_provider.py for state_scope -- one hit, in the docstring.
next_action: Refuse the publish where the incoming partition set does not cover the set it replaces. The guard belongs in publish, not in the caller, because publish is what destroys.
Author the requirement this needs; the pipeline stages have none.

bug.title: The agent's self-escalation condition is void beside an unconditioned Owner grant
bug.description:
claudeCodeAgent holds the custom role chatHealthyAgent on the PipeLineServices subscription WITH its assignment condition applied and intact. The condition forbids role-assignment writes and deletes for six role-definition ids, including Owner and Contributor, so the identity cannot grant itself back a capability that was taken away. It is a well-made control.

The same identity also holds plain Owner on the same subscription with NO condition. Owner already grants role-assignment write. Azure unions a principal's assignments, so the constrained path and an unconstrained path to the same action sit side by side and the condition withholds nothing.

The control is not badly designed. It is defeated additively, by a second grant that nothing compares it against -- which is why a reading of either assignment alone reports a healthy posture. The lesson generalises: enumerate the union of a principal's grants, then check the union.
test_success_criteria: No identity holds an unconditioned grant that supplies an action a condition on another of its grants withholds.
Boolean test: for each principal, union the actions of every assignment; the union MUST NOT contain an action that any condition on that principal forbids.
bug.reproduction:
1. List role assignments for the claudeCodeAgent service principal on the PipeLineServices subscription.
2. Observe two: chatHealthyAgent carrying a condition, and Owner carrying none.
3. Read the condition -- it names six role-definition ids for role-assignment write and delete.
4. Owner's actions include role-assignment write, unconditioned.
next_action: Decide whether the unconditioned Owner grant on this identity is intentional. If it is, the finding is that the condition is redundant and should be removed rather than left to imply a constraint. If it is not, removing Owner makes the existing condition load-bearing.
Either way this is one role assignment, not a programme.

bug.title: Deploy build context ships files that no runtime code path uses
bug.description:
CORRECTED 2026-09-10 after running this bug's own reproduction. The mechanism this bug named no longer exists and the defect it names does. Those are two different facts and the record had merged them.

GONE: the wholesale subtree copy. _copy_tree is defined and called from nowhere; _findcare_source_set survives only inside a docstring saying it was replaced by _source_set_for, which reads huggingface_source_set from the deployment record. The build now stages an enumerated file list.

NOT GONE: the criterion. A local build of target_hf_space_findcare_backend stages 82 files, of which 31 are under the legacy tree, and these are reached by no runtime code path on that target:
  Code/Shared/llm_client.py, which no file imports anywhere
  Code/Shared/prompt_system_maker.py, a prompt-authoring tool
  backend/domain/shared/safety/safety_service.py, whose is_emergency has no call site
  backend/README.md, documentation shipped into a container
  Code/Shared/ops/certs/evalcare.crt -- FindCare needs shared.crt to verify the gateway signature and its own certificate; EvaluateCare's has no reader here

So the selection changed and the selected set did not. The record now enumerates the dead files instead of walking a subtree that contained them. Fixing how a thing is chosen is not the same as fixing what is chosen, and an enumerated list of the wrong files is harder to notice than a subtree walk, because it reads as deliberate.
test_success_criteria: Every file present in a target's build context is reached by a runtime code path on that target. No file present in a build context is unused by the runtime that target hosts.
bug.reproduction:
1. Build local: build_chathealthy.py --env local --target target_hf_space_findcare_backend
2. Find every staged file under the legacy tree in build/target_hf_space_findcare_backend -- observe 31.
3. For each, search the FindCare runtime for an import or a read of it. The five named above have none.
4. Search for a call to _copy_tree in the devops directory -- observe a definition and no call, confirming the mechanism in the original description is gone.
next_action: Author a new REQ on EPIC-008-F-012 capturing the bidirectional exact-truth contract for files per target — analog to REQ-B-008 (env vars) and REQ-B-009 (entitlements). Re-link this bug's req_id when the REQ exists.
Replace the wholesale subtree-copy mechanism with an explicit per-target file list driven by deployment_architecture.json. The build stages only what the manifest enumerates for that target.
Implement, then bring this bug to closed.

bug.title: Cloudflare users are a second identity registry outside the firm's IAM
bug.description:
EPIC-002-F-003-S-008 states that every authenticating component has one canonical identity and that every identity, machine or human, lives in a single registry. IdentityCatalog in deployment_architecture.json holds seven entries, all Entra, all Azure-facing. No Cloudflare identity appears in it.

Cloudflare account users are authenticating actors holding real authority: DNS, the WAF, the Pages deployment, and the edge that fronts the whole application. They are governed by a separate account's own user list, with their own credentials and their own second factor -- which is why EPIC-002-F-001-S-005 exists as a requirement to enable MFA for all Cloudflare account users. That requirement only makes sense for users outside the registry; an identity inside it would take its second factor from conditional access.

The three tests the security framework applies elsewhere all fail here. A Cloudflare account administrator can switch off the MFA the backlog asks for, so the constrained party can lift the constraint. Nothing in the firm's record declares who those users are, so no independent reading can contradict a claim about them. And no party other than the firm can check any of it.

Cloudflare Zero Trust federates with Entra over OIDC or SAML, so this is a configuration gap rather than a platform limitation.
test_success_criteria: Every actor who can authenticate to Cloudflare appears in the firm's identity registry and authenticates through it.
The entitlement report enumerates Cloudflare authority alongside Entra, Azure and Atlas, read from Cloudflare's own API rather than from a declaration.
bug.reproduction:
1. Read IdentityCatalog in deployment_architecture.json -- seven entries, none of them a Cloudflare identity.
2. Read EPIC-002-F-001-S-005 in agile_backlog.json -- an approved requirement to enable MFA for all Cloudflare account users.
3. Run the entitlement report and observe that Cloudflare appears in the Scope prose as a protected component and in no section that enumerates who holds rights over it.
next_action: Decide whether Cloudflare federates into Entra. It is new architecture and it supersedes at least one approved story, so the requirement is the operator's to author.
Until then the entitlement report cannot answer who can change the edge, and that gap should be stated in the report rather than absent from it.
